author: Sven Oakbarrel, formerly of the East Gate
pages:
#Thirty Years at the Gate

I stood at the East Gate for thirty years. I have seen jarls come and go, dragons fly over, and more lost travellers than I can count. People think guarding a gate is dull work. They are right. These are the memoirs of a dull man.

#My Early Ambitions

I did not always wish to be a guard. As a lad I dreamed of adventure: ruins and treasure, ancient tombs, monsters slain in the dark. I trained with sword and shield. I could hit a target at fifty paces with a bow.

Then something happened to my knee. I will not go into details. Every guard in the north has heard the story already and I am weary of the jokes.

#Things Travellers Say

"I am here to see the jarl." Everyone is here to see the jarl. The jarl does not want to see any of you.

"Do you know who I am?" No.

"I used to be a guard like you." Then you know how this ends, friend. Move along.

#On Thieves

Most thieves are not clever. They are merely optimistic. They walk out of the market with three apples and a stolen silver goblet under their tunic, clanking at every step, and they look shocked when we stop them.

The clever ones we never see, which is how we know they are clever.

#Retirement

I now keep bees on a little farm beyond the walls. The bees are better company than most of the travellers I met, and they only sting you when you deserve it.

My knee still aches when the weather turns. I do not tell anyone why. Some stories are better left untold, especially the ones everyone already knows.
